specific_checks: The two-sided CDF envelope max(u/K,1-K+Ku) crosses at K/(K+1) and integrates to 1/(K+1). The monotone quantile contribution and feasible deletion justify the offline bound, including ties. Its one-coordinate nearly constant continuous-weight family proves sharpness of that filter, not online impossibility.

Under a common positive weight interval [a,alpha a], every-order greedy acceptance yields a maximal independent set of positive passing candidates and hence their full rank. The pointwise alpha comparison establishes the stated restricted online ratio and includes the full-data adversary. The epsilon/one deterministic example genuinely prevents removing the support condition for that rule.

The uniform-matroid flag counterexample has r-1 singleton layers independent of online Bernoulli values, plus one capacity-one last layer. The less-than-two reward bound and Chebyshev lower bound of order r for OPT apply to actual K=1 independent coordinates.

W119 uses a fixed family before focal mask exposure and a heterogeneous product bound, allowing adaptive selection only within that family. Parent checked the original source transfer conditioning and safe-label baseline endpoint. The weighted rank/error and full hybrid-pivotal chain remains assigned for independent universal-proof audit.

The combined coefficient BZ/r is a convex combination of 1/r,1,r with nonnegative coefficients summing to one, so its K bound does pay one K for the leading mass. This does not cancel the test-rate, rank-conversion, path or small-group costs retained in BUD.

PIV is a finite product-law differentiation identity for a decreasing event. Adaptive transcript integration and the aggregate XI bound are distinct: XI is explicitly unpaid. EX restricts one marginal-preserving fixed-thinning invariant, not all online policies.
